plan.title: Unify dashboard menus, popovers, and semantic color styling
plan.author: overdeck/auto-start

narratives.Problem:
## Problem

Several dashboard surfaces bypass the shared menu, popup, and semantic-color vocabulary. The result is visible drift: the same overflow action changes density and shadow by route, operational warnings use unrelated colors, and some system popovers look like separate products.

This issue is a bounded refinement of the incumbent Command Deck design. Preserve behavior and information architecture; consolidate one-off styling into existing shared primitives and semantic tokens.

## Incumbent visual truth

Use these as the baseline:

- `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/shared/ContextMenu.tsx`
- `src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/IssueActionMenu/IssueActionMenu.tsx`
- the semantic tokens and theme definitions already used by those surfaces
- `src/dashboard/frontend/PRODUCT.md`: calm under load, dense but legible, one interaction vocabulary

The Issue Actions menu may still need structural simplification, but do not copy its admin-matrix density into simple context menus. Reuse its shared popup vocabulary where the interaction role matches.

## High-confidence inconsistencies

### 1. Conversation and pane menus

`src/dashboard/frontend/src/components/CommandDeck/styles/command-deck.module.css` defines a legacy menu skin with custom width, padding, radii, raw shadow, and item sizing. It is consumed by:

- `CommandDeck/ConversationActionMenu.tsx`
- `CommandDeck/ConversationRow.tsx`
- `chat/ConversationPanel.tsx`
- `Stage/PaneTabMenu.tsx`

Move matching context-menu interactions onto the shared menu primitive/tokens. Preserve positioning, keyboard behavior, destructive-state treatment, and route-specific actions.

### 2. Deacon pause state

`DeaconPauseToggle.tsx` hard-codes `sky-*` colors for an operational pause/alert state while neighboring operational surfaces use semantic warning tokens. Replace palette-specific classes with the correct semantic state and verify all themes and compact/expanded states.

### 3. Planning surfaces

`PlanDialog.tsx` and `PlanSetupScreen.tsx` use hard-coded purple-to-blue gradients and purple borders. Bring them into the established `primary` / `signal-review` vocabulary without flattening hierarchy or obscuring the primary planning action.

### 4. Cloister restart popover

`CloisterStatusBar.tsx` uses inline width, radius, raw RGBA shadow, and fallback colors inside `SystemMenu.tsx`. Replace the one-off frame with shared popup tokens or a shared component. Preserve restart state, confirmation, focus return, and constrained viewport placement.

## Secondary audit-and-fix scope

Review these while the shared vocabulary is in hand. Fix raw styling when an existing semantic token expresses the same meaning; document a narrow exception when the color is genuine domain encoding:

- `CommandDeck/ActivityView/index.tsx`: raw indigo/purple/green/pink values and card side accents.
- `CommandPalette.tsx`: hard-coded Tailwind category palettes.
- `BacklogSequencerPage.tsx`: legacy aliases, arbitrary `color-mix`, custom chips, and a pass picker that does not match menu semantics.

## Intentional exemptions

- God View's scoped neon theme and Space Grotesk typography.
- Terminal presentation.
- Kanban and IssueCard status stripes when color carries stable task-state meaning.

Do not normalize these as collateral cleanup.

## Requirements

- [ ] Classify each finding as a missing token, one-off implementation, conceptual mismatch, or local defect before editing.
- [ ] Reuse shared primitives for same-role menus and popovers; do not introduce a second replacement primitive.
- [ ] Replace palette literals with semantic tokens wherever the meaning already exists.
- [ ] Preserve action availability, ordering, copy, destructive confirmation, positioning, and disabled/loading behavior.
- [ ] Preserve visible focus, menu semantics, keyboard navigation, focus return, and screen-reader names.
- [ ] Verify light and dark themes at narrow and desktop widths.
- [ ] Use Playwright screenshots and inspect them directly; do not delegate visual acceptance to the operator.
- [ ] Run the Impeccable detector after edits and resolve new applicable findings in one bounded correction pass.
- [ ] Add or update focused component tests for interaction and semantic behavior.
- [ ] Update the dashboard style documentation to identify the canonical context-menu/popover primitive and intentional exemptions.

## Acceptance criteria

- Same-role context menus have consistent padding, radius, type scale, item states, and shadow across issue, conversation, and pane surfaces.
- Deacon pause and planning states use theme-aware semantic colors with acceptable contrast.
- The Cloister restart flow uses the common popup vocabulary and remains fully keyboard-operable.
- Secondary surfaces contain no unexplained palette literals where a semantic token exists.
- Desktop and narrow screenshots show no clipping, accidental density changes, or hierarchy regressions in either theme.
- Relevant frontend tests, typecheck, build, and detector checks pass.
